evals.prompt: Why is the derived S3 bucket name `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` vulnerable to pre-registration ('bucket-squatting') by a third party, and how does Step 5 of `setup-security-agent` defend against it during both `aws s3api head-bucket` probing and `aws s3api create-bucket` (including the difference between `BucketAlreadyExists` vs `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` and `us-east-1` vs non-`us-east-1` `LocationConstraint`)?
evals.expected_output: Explains that AWS Account IDs and regions are non-secret and publicly derivable from ARNs/ECR URIs, so an attacker can pre-register `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` in their own AWS account. Details Step 5: (1) probing via `aws s3api head-bucket --bucket "$BUCKET" --expected-bucket-owner "$ACCOUNT"` where `200` reuses the bucket, `404` sets `NEED_CREATE=1`, and `403 Forbidden` is treated as **FATAL** (foreign-owned bucket -> abort immediately, never upload), and (2) creating via `aws s3api create-bucket` (no `LocationConstraint` in `us-east-1`, `--create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint="$REGION"` in other regions), treating `BucketAlreadyExists` as **FATAL** (foreign account owns the name) while `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` is a safe no-op, followed by re-asserting ownership with `head-bucket --expected-bucket-owner "$ACCOUNT"`, enabling all 4 `BlockPublicAccess` flags, and applying a 30-day `AutoDeleteUploads` lifecycle rule.
expectations: Explains why `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` is predictable (Account ID and region are non-secret) and how `--expected-bucket-owner "$ACCOUNT"` prevents uploading code to a foreign-owned squatted bucket
Distinguishes `head-bucket` status codes: `404` -> create bucket (`NEED_CREATE=1`), vs `403 Forbidden` -> **FATAL** bucket-squatting indicator (abort immediately and never upload)

Distinguishes `create-bucket` error codes: `BucketAlreadyExists` -> **FATAL** (owned by another AWS account, abort) vs `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` -> safe idempotent no-op, and notes that `us-east-1` omits `LocationConstraint` while other regions require `LocationConstraint="$REGION"`

Includes post-creation hardening: re-verifying ownership with `head-bucket --expected-bucket-owner "$ACCOUNT"`, enabling all 4 `PublicAccessBlockConfiguration` flags, and applying the 30-day `AutoDeleteUploads` lifecycle expiration rule

evals.prompt: Suppose `.security-agent/config.json` is missing and `aws securityagent list-agent-spaces` returns two existing Agent Spaces: `as-111 (payments-sec)` and `as-222 (platform-sec)`. (1) May the agent automatically pick the first Agent Space (`as-111`)? (2) Once the user selects `as-222`, how does Step 6 register `SecurityAgentScanRole` and `security-agent-scans-123456789012-us-east-1` onto `as-222` without wiping out existing roles and buckets already attached to `as-222`?
evals.expected_output: States (1) **Never auto-select** an Agent Space when existing ones are found — show the list (`name` + `id`) to the user and ask whether to reuse one of them or create a new one (`create-agent-space --name security-scans`), waiting for their answer; and (2) in Step 6, call `aws securityagent batch-get-agent-spaces --agent-space-ids as-222`, read `agentSpaces[0].awsResources.iamRoles` and `awsResources.s3Buckets`, merge the new role ARN and bucket name into the existing lists (deduplicating), and call `aws securityagent update-agent-space --agent-space-id as-222 --name platform-sec --aws-resources iamRoles=[...],s3Buckets=[...]`.
expectations: Enforces the strict rule: **Never auto-select** an Agent Space when existing spaces are returned by `list-agent-spaces` — display their names and IDs and ask the user whether to reuse one or create a new one

Explains Step 6's read-merge-write pattern: call `batch-get-agent-spaces --agent-space-ids as-222` to inspect `agentSpaces[0].awsResources.iamRoles` and `awsResources.s3Buckets`, append the role ARN and bucket name if missing, and call `update-agent-space` with the merged lists so existing resources on the shared Agent Space are preserved

evals.prompt: Why does `.security-agent/config.json` only store `{"agent_space_id": "as-xxxxx", "region": "us-east-1"}` (plus optional `code_reviews` / `target_domains` maps) rather than storing `account_id`, `role_arn`, and `s3_bucket`? And what should you tell a user who asks to use a custom role name `MyCustomScannerRole` and custom bucket `my-company-custom-scans`?
evals.expected_output: Explains convention-over-config: `ACCOUNT`, `arn:aws:iam::${ACCOUNT}:role/SecurityAgentScanRole`, and `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` are deterministic and derived on every invocation so they can never drift out of sync with active credentials/account, whereas `agent_space_id` is stored because an account can have multiple Agent Spaces. Explains that if a user requests custom role/bucket names, the agent must inform them that the scan, diff-scan, threat-model, and pentest skills derive `SecurityAgentScanRole` and `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` by convention rather than reading them from `config.json`, so they must either accept the conventional defaults or extend the skills.
expectations: Explains why `config.json` is kept minimal: deriving `ACCOUNT`, `SecurityAgentScanRole`, and `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` dynamically prevents configuration drift across sessions or credential changes, while `agent_space_id` is stored to avoid prompting which Agent Space to use every time

Explains what to tell a user requesting a custom role or bucket name: the companion skills (`scanning-with-aws-security-agent`, `diff-scanning-with-aws-security-agent`, `threat-modeling-with-aws-security-agent`, `pentesting-with-aws-security-agent`) derive `SecurityAgentScanRole` and `security-agent-scans-${ACCOUNT}-${REGION}` by convention rather than reading them from `config.json`
